text:
santiago: Heads-up — we're seeing a P99 tail latency spike on hosted continuous-batcher since ~08:15 UTC. p50 ~12ms, p95 ~40ms, p99 ~560ms. Rolling window shows oscillation every ~30s.
maya: noticed the same on dashboard. throughput steady, but request latencies jump and then recover in a sawtooth.
jonathan: any rollout around that time?
santiago: no platform deploys, but kernel-selector config pushed to prod at 07:50 last night (experiment weight change).
lee: I'm pulling profiler snapshots now. can someone paste the deployment id?
perf-bot: Profiler capture started for service=continuous-batcher pool=cb-prod-1 duration=60s id=prof-2412345678-1
jonathan: thanks. looking at admission logs — microbatch sizes are swinging between 1 and 8 frequently.
maya: that would explain extra kernel churn. kernel selector flips cause different kernel code paths causing CPU/GPU warmup and KV miss patterns.
santiago: stack from one of the slow samples: ```
# slow sample
select_kernel_for_seq_len(seq_len=512) -> fused_gpt_kernel_v2
kv_cache_lookup -> miss -> allocate_shard_entry
continuous_batcher::admit -> create_microbatch(size=1)
launch_kernel(fused_gpt_kernel_v2)
```
jonathan: and a fast sample: ```
select_kernel_for_seq_len(seq_len=128) -> attention_opt_kernel_v1
kv_cache_lookup -> hit -> append_to_microbatch(size=8)
launch_kernel(attention_opt_kernel_v1)
```
lee: profiler flame shows a 3x increase in time inside select_kernel_for_seq_len when seq_len distribution is noisy. kernel_selector does an expensive heuristic involving histograms and nearest-neighbor fallback.
maya: is the KV cache eviction rate high? ops-bot: kvcache.evictions: 4200/min (baseline 400/min), kvcache.hits dropped from 92% to 71% since 08:10 UTC.
jonathan: noisy neighbor tenant TID=team-x had a sudden spike in short sequences around 08:12 — lots of small requests causing microbatch fragmentation.
santiago: so hypothesis: tenant bursts of short seqs cause microbatch size collapse, selector flips kernels for small vs long seqs, and KV cache eviction churn increases, adding tail latency.
lee: can we reproduce on staging with a mixed workload? I'll run a 30m replay with a 70/30 short/long pattern and enable the new kernel-selector weight.
maya: short-term mitigation: clamp min_microbatch_size to 4 for this pool, and increase kvcache per-shard threshold. That should make batching more stable.
jonathan: agree. also add a debounce on kernel-selector flips (only change kernel if >N consecutive batches pick the new kernel).
santiago: I can patch admission to add min_microbatch_size=4 as a hotfix in prod. any objections?
lee: +1 from perf perspective. might slightly increase latency for tiny requests but should stabilize p99.
maya: I'll prepare the rollout and a revert plan.
deploy-bot: /deploy cb-prod-1 --patch admission=min_microbatch_size=4 --ticket=INC-2412
deploy-bot: Rolling out patch to 10% -> 50% -> 100%, starting 08:42 UTC. monitor p99.
perf-bot: profiler capture queued id=prof-2412345678-2 start=08:45 duration=120s
maya: after 20m at 50% we see p99 drop from 560ms to ~180ms, kvcache.hits up to 84%. microbatch size median moved from 2->5.
jonathan: kernel-selector flip rate metric (changes/min) down from 18/min -> 3/min.
santiago: solid. what's the plan for a longer fix?
lee: action items: 1) add debounce to kernel-selector, 2) make kvcache per-tenant buffers adaptive to short-seq bursts, 3) add admission jitter to avoid synchronized admission collapses, 4) improve selector heuristic to consider recent seq_len variance.
maya: I'll open PRs: rb/continuous-batcher/patches - one for debounce + tests, one for kvcache sizing.
jonathan: also add a lightweight metric: microbatch_entropy (Shannon over batch sizes) so we can alert on high fragmentation early.
santiago: thanks. can we keep the hotfix for at least 12 hours then revert if no regressions?
lee: yes. I'll run the staging replay with new debounce and kvcache sizing before we commit to permanent change.
ops-bot: Alert threshold adjusted: cb-prod-1 p99 > 250ms for 3m -> page oncall.
maya: noted. will follow up with a summary in incidents later.
santiago: one more note — customers on Dedicated with strict tail SLOs might want opt-in to hard min_microbatch. we'll add a config flag.
jonathan: copying to docs: perf/continuous-batcher/notes.md later. good catch team. :thumbsup:
lee: summarizing: root cause = workload-driven microbatch fragmentation + kernel-selector oscillation + KV eviction spike. remediate = hotfix clamp + longer-term selector/kvcache/admission changes.
santiago: closing the thread, will post incident summary in ~2h. thanks everyone.
